Subject: Post-call: Private VPC deployment options & next steps

Hi Amit / Lina,

Thanks again for the call today — good to meet the FinTrak team. Quick recap and the network info we need to progress the Private VPC deployment:

Summary of what we heard
- You want a Private deployment (customer VPC) to meet your data isolation and compliance requirements.
- Preference: AWS-based deployment; lean toward VPC peering rather than PrivateLink for now, but want to confirm tradeoffs.
- Key constraints: static egress IPs for allowlisting, internal firewall rules, and a dedicated subnet for the Redwood connector.

Immediate ask from our side (can you confirm / share?):
1) AWS account ID(s) and desired region(s) for hosting (example: us-east-1).
2) Which connectivity method do you prefer: VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink? If undecided, tell us why (e.g., cross-account restrictions, managed NAT, etc.).
3) CIDR(s) you can allocate for the connector (we typically ask for /28 or /27 depending on scale).
4) IP allowlist / firewall escalation process: email + ticketing contact.
5) Any compliance docs we should factor in (specific controls beyond SOC2)?

I attached our Private VPC checklist to help your network team see the standard requirements. Once you confirm the items above, I’ll loop in our infra lead (Sean) for a technical deep-dive and we can lock a 30–45m slot to go through peering setup and routing.

Proposed next steps
- You share the items above (can reply inline).
- I schedule a technical session with Sean + our deployment engineer.
- We send a draft mutual action plan with dates and deliverables.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short follow-up tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Post-call: Private VPC deployment options & next steps

Great, thanks for the quick responses + the network export. Looping in Sean (infra) and Rachel (solutions) so we can set up the technical session and align on routing/allowlist details.

Answers to network questions:
- Allowlisting: we provide stable egress IP addresses for the connector; you can allowlist those IPs on your firewall. For initial scale with a /28 we typically provide 4–8 egress IPs.
- Ports: outbound TCP 443 (HTTPS) is sufficient for API traffic; SSH is not required for normal operation. If you plan to use our remote support connector we can discuss a separate management channel.
- Peering & routing: yes, we ask that you add a route in your route table to the connector CIDR pointing at the peering connection. No special NAT required unless you expect asymmetric routing — we recommend a simple route via the peering attachment.

Recommended next steps (from engineering):
1) Schedule a 45m technical deep-dive: agenda — peering setup, routing changes, security (egress IPs), and test plan.
2) Share a small sample security allowlist template — we’ll provide the egress IPs and exact ports in advance.
3) Exchange timeline and sign-off owners so we can create a mutual action plan.

I attached our peering recommendations doc and a simple diagram to show the minimal routing changes. Please propose 2–3 times for next week and Sean will pick a slot.

Best,
Marissa Cole
